title: WPSB/297/2015 of Deepak Kumar Yadav AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 297 of 2015
Deepak Kumar Yadav and another ......... Petitioners

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ......... Respondents
Present: Mr. Shobhit Saharia, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. Ravindra Singh Bisht, Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent no.1.
Ms. Beena Pande, Additional Standing Counsel for the State
of U.P./respondent no.2.
Mr. Lok Pal Singh, Advocate for respondent no.3.

Coram : Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J.
JUDGMENT
Date: 3rd August, 2015
K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)

Petitioners have approached this Court feeling
aggrieved by three orders; firstly there is order dated 10.08.2006
(Annexure-9); then there is order dated 10.06.2009 (Annexure-10)
and finally there is order dated 24.06.2005 (Annexure-13).
2. Petitioners were directly recruited as Assistant
Engineers (Civil) in the year 1990 and they were substantively
appointed by orders dated 20.09.1990 and 06.07.1992 respectively.
The question relates to seniority of the petitioners on the one hand
and the 3rd respondent. The 3rd respondent was initially appointed
as Junior Engineer on ad hoc basis in the year 1983. Subsequently,
according to him, he has been absorbed in a substantive capacity
w.e.f. 1st March, 1988. The 3rd respondent was confirmed on
04.04.1992 but w.e.f. 01.03.1990. According to the 3rd respondent,
he was entitled for consideration in the first promotional exercise
after 01.03.1990. He filed claim petition before the Public Services
Tribunal, which was initially disposed of by directing consideration
of his case. It was considered and the prayer was rejected. He filed

2
another Claim Petition No. 01 of 2001. Even though initially it was
dismissed as barred by the constructive res judicata pursuant to
judgment of the High Court, the matter was considered on merits
culminating in Annexure-6 order dated 16.07.2003. Therein the
Tribunal found that he is entitled to be considered for the vacancies
in 1990, and if not in 1990, he should be considered for the
vacancies of Assistant Engineer in 1991. Order dated 31.03.2004
ensued, wherein his claim was rejected. Contempt Petitions were
filed in respect of the earlier order of the Tribunal as also the order
dated 16.07.2003. That culminated in Annexure 9, which is one of
the impugned orders. The said order is essentially an order, by
which the Tribunal took the view that the contempt is to be
proceeded as against respondent Nos. 1 & 3. In the course of the
discussion, the Tribunal held as follows:
"10. Petitioner has nothing to do with the promotion of Shri
 Pathak as it is creation of respondents. The
 respondents should have created a supernumerary post
 for the petitioner and promoted him as per the
 direction of the Tribunal.
11. In view of the above discussion, we are of the view
 that Respondent No. 1 who was appointing authority at
 the relevant time and Respondent No. 3 who is holding
 same post at present are prima facie guilty for willful
 disobedience of the judgment and order of the Tribunal
 and therefore, liable to be charged under Section 12 (1)
 of Contempt of Court Act, 1971."
3. Thereafter, according to the petitioners, Annexure-10
is issued, which is annexed in the impugned order. According to the
petitioners, therein the Authority proceeded to state, inter alia, that
in compliance with the order dated 10.08.2006 (Annexure-9) an ex
cadre post is being created to accommodate the 3rd respondent.
Subsequently, coming to the last of the impugned orders, which is
of the year of 2015, it is an order by which objections filed by the
petitioners against the tentative seniority list were rejected and the

3
petitioners were placed below the 3rd respondent. In the meantime,
there were promotions effected to the higher categories.
4. We heard Shri Shobhit Saharia, learned counsel for the
petitioners, Shri Lok Pal Singh, who appeard at the admission stage
on behalf of the party respondent and also the Government Pleader
for the State of U.P.
5. Shri Lok Pal Singh, in fact, would point that the
contempt proceedings have been dropped. He drew our attention to
the following order passed by this Court in Writ Petition (S/B) 68
of 2007 on 01.04.2009 :
 "On this petition coming up for orders today, Mrs.
Beena Pande, learned Standing Counsel appearing for the
petitioners, seeks leave of this Court to withdraw this writ
petition in so far as prayer no. (i) relating to challenge to the
impugned judgment dated 16th July, 2003 passed by the
Public Services Tribunal, Uttarakhand, Dehradun in Claim
Petition No. 01 of 2001: Arun Kumar Goel vs. State and
others is concerned. The writ petition, accordingly, in so far
as the aforesaid prayer no. (i) is concerned, is hereby
dismissed as withdrawn and the aforesaid judgment of the
Tribunal is affirmed by this Court.
 Prayer no. (ii) in the writ petition relates to an order
dated 19.03.2007 passed by Public Services Tribunal,
Uttarakhand, Dehradun in Contempt Petition No. C/100 of
2004. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and find
that in view of the fact that the writ petition is being
dismissed as withdrawn qua prayer no. (i), the proceedings in
the aforesaid contempt matter should not be allowed to
continue.
 The order dated 19.03.2007 accordingly is hereby set
aside and the aforesaid contempt proceedings pending in the
Tribunal are dropped."
6. It is the contention of Shri Shobhit Saharia, learned
counsel for the petitioners that the statement in Annexure-9 that an
ex cadre post should be created can only be treated as an
observation and there was no direction and also it is submitted that
a direction can not be issued.

4
7. He would also on being alerted to the order of this
Court point out that by the judgment of this Court dated
01.04.2009 the contempt proceedings have been dropped and
Annexure-9 can not survive the dropping of the contempt
proceedings. Therefore, he would also submit that in the light of the
same, there is no basis for stating in Annexure-10 that in
compliance with Annexure-9 the post will be created.
8. We are of the view that the petitioners are to be
relegated to approach to the Public Services Tribunal, wherein it is
open to the parties to raise all contentions. We only observe that in
case it is found necessary for the petitioners to challenge Annexure-9, we leave it open to the petitioner if that situation arises.
9. The writ petition stands disposed of.
 (U.C. Dhyani, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 03.08.2015 03.08.2015
P. Singh
